title: FuzeFront AppManifest
description: The declarative document describing how the host mounts and chromes an app. Stored on the app row, served back on read, and the single shared type across UI / backend / tests.

menuLabel.description: Label shown in the application menu / launcher (e.g. "Market").

builtin.description: Shipped with the platform; cannot be deleted, only suspended.

roles.description: Roles permitted to see/activate the app. Empty = all members.

AppManifest.description: The declarative document describing how the host mounts and chromes an app. Stored on the app row, served back on read, and the single shared type across UI / backend / tests.

menuLabel.description: Label shown in the application menu / launcher (e.g. "Market").

builtin.description: Shipped with the platform; cannot be deleted, only suspended.

roles.description: Roles permitted to see/activate the app. Empty = all members.

Slug.description: URL-safe unique identifier, immutable once registered.

AppMode.description: `portal` — mounted inside the host shell at `/app/:slug` with chrome. `standalone` — rendered without portal chrome on its own host/path.

Icon.description: App icon — either an emoji glyph or an image URL.

value.description: The emoji character, or an https URL to the icon image.

Integration.description: How the host loads/mounts the app.

remoteEntry.description: FULL Module-Federation remote entry URL, e.g. `https://clock.example.com/remoteEntry.js`. Required when `type = module-federation`. This freezes the legacy base-vs-entry ambiguity: the value is the complete entry URL, NOT a base.

scope.description: MF remote scope/name. Required for module-federation.

module.description: Exposed module path, e.g. `./ClockApp`. Required for module-federation.

MenuItem.description: An app-declared menu item (for chrome substitution or app section).

route.description: in-app route the item navigates to

Chrome.description: How the host's chrome behaves while this app is active. Ignored for `mode = standalone` (standalone apps render with no portal chrome).

menu.description: `host` — keep the portal side menu (app may still push runtime items). `substitute` — the app provides its OWN full side menu; the host yields its portal menu and renders `items` instead. The host always retains a minimal "return to portal" affordance so the user is never trapped.

items.description: App-declared menu items, used when `menu = substitute`.

Nav.description: Where the app sits in the host's side menu. The app DECLARES its own placement here rather than the platform holding a central ordering table, so onboarding a product never requires a FuzeFront edit.

order.description: Rank WITHIN the section, ascending. Ties break on `slug` so ordering is always total and stable. Leave unset (999) to sort after apps that care.

NavSection.description: The app's place in the company's day-to-day lifecycle. The host groups the side menu by this, in the order declared here: steer -> plan -> build -> sell -> serve -> measure -> operate. Apps that do not declare one fall into `platform` (last).

Routing.description: Routing for the app. `host` applies to standalone only.

path.description: Path the app is reachable at. For portal apps this is informational (host mounts at `/app/:slug`); for standalone it is the routed path.

host.description: Standalone-only: a dedicated host (e.g. `clock.fuzefront.com`). When omitted, standalone apps are path-based under the main app host.

Infra.description: Platform infrastructure the (typically standalone) app opts into. Portal apps implicitly get auth + api; this block is mainly meaningful for standalone apps that selectively use FuzeFront infra.

deployOnFuzeInfra.description: Deployed via the FuzeInfra GitOps pipeline
